items: Diagnose Your Plateau: Answer the five classification questions about weeks in deficit, hunger levels, gym performance, scale jumps, and sleep quality to identify your dominant plateau type.
Diagnose Your Plateau: Write down your answers and look for patterns — if you answered yes to constant hunger and waking exhausted, your dominant plateau is likely hormonal.
Diagnose Your Plateau: If your gym performance has plateaued or declined and you feel more sedentary outside workouts, your dominant plateau is neural adaptation requiring different interventions.
Diagnose Your Plateau: When the scale jumps 1-3kg overnight after eating more carbs or changing sodium intake, recognize this as a water retention plateau, not actual fat gain.
Calculate Your Metabolism: Multiply your current body weight in kg by 22 if you're female or 24 if you're male to estimate your baseline resting metabolic rate.
Calculate Your Metabolism: Apply your activity multiplier to your RMR to determine your true maintenance calories, which have likely decreased since you started dieting.
Calculate Your Metabolism: Subtract 300-500 calories from your recalculated maintenance to set an accurate deficit, accounting for metabolic adaptation that occurred during your weight loss.

Calculate Your Metabolism: Compare your current calorie target to what you started with — if you've reduced intake significantly without recalculating, you may be eating at maintenance instead of deficit.
Execute Interventions: Plan a strategic refeed with 150-200% of your normal carbohydrate intake for 24-48 hours to elevate leptin and thyroid hormones and signal your body that starvation has ended.
Execute Interventions: Monitor your refeed carefully — a true refeed resets hormones and accelerates fat loss, while an uncontrolled binge simply adds calories without metabolic benefits.
Execute Interventions: After refeeding, return immediately to your calculated deficit on Monday rather than extending the higher eating period, since extended surplus undoes your caloric progress.

Execute Interventions: Implement the 48-hour plateau response system when the scale stalls for more than two weeks, using your plateau classification to choose the right intervention instead of guessing.
